narrative_purpose: Carries the chapter's Earth-turn in one image: the same pore, the same job, two different water bills — because the only thing that changed is the air on the other side of the opening.
subject: A split-panel comparison of two leaf-surface pores in extreme close-up, each formed by a pair of curved kidney-shaped cells. Left panel: the two cells are bowed far apart leaving a wide open slit, and a thick billowing plume of vapour streams up out of it while only a thin trickle of small particles descends into it. Right panel: the same two cells are almost touching, leaving only a narrow crack, from which just a single thin thread of vapour escapes — while a dense crowd of small particles presses down into the crack from above.
scene: Two paired surface studies side by side against deep dark, divided by a thin band of haze, each showing a patch of waxy leaf epidermis with one pore at its centre.
camera: A straight-on paired close view from just above the leaf surface, both pores at identical magnification.
light: The vapour plumes are the brightest elements, lit from within; the leaf surface catches a low waxy sheen; deep indigo shadow in the pore openings.
palette: Void-indigo ground and deep teal epidermis; the vapour plumes in biolum magenta; the descending gas particles in Pandora cyan, sparse on the left and densely crowded on the right.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, a microscopist's surface study rendered as illustration.
detail_level: Crisp on the guard-cell shapes, the width of each opening, and the very different plume volumes; surrounding epidermis softer.
composition: Two equal vertical panels with a dark central seam, each pore centred low in its panel with the plume rising into open dark space above it, leaving quiet regions for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with magenta reserved for the water being lost; the asymmetry between the two panels — wide pore with heavy loss versus narrow pore with almost none — is the entire point and must be unmistakable.
